records.summary: The innermost layer of the Convergence, Synthetica is where the first inklings of differentiation emerge from Non Duality. It's the realm of synthesis, where the initial combinations of essence and form take shape. Here, realities are in their nascent state, just beginning to intertwine and interweave. It's a realm of potential, where the future shapes of the Sea of Realities start to coalesce.

The outermost layer of the Convergence, Translimina stands as the gateway to the Sea of Realities. Here, the fusion processes of Meldara begin to stabilize, and distinct realities start to crystallize. However, the boundaries are still permeable, and realities can drift in and out, leading to ephemeral and transient manifestations. It's a liminal space, bridging the chaotic heart of the Convergence with the more structured expanse of the Sea of Realities. think backrooms ---

Translimina is a subtle and often unnoticeable layer of reality, blending seamlessly with the environments of the worlds it connects to. Entry into this liminal dimension can occur through natural phenomena, unintentional mishaps, or deliberate magical or planar manipulation, but the most unsettling entrances are the ones that appear ordinary—almost too ordinary.
Translimina can, with difficulty, be used to move between nearby realities. However, finding an exit into a specific world is challenging.

records.proposedName: Uneksia: The Boundary Between Dreams and Reality
records.summary: Description: Uneksia is the threshold realm where dream states lose coherence, becoming less stable as they begin to dissolve into the unknown expanses beyond. Existing as the “shore” of the Dreaming Realms, Uneksia is a place where elements of waking life and dream-like visions intertwine, creating a half-real, half-dream environment. ---

"The Empire's Brightest Jewel—and its most volatile spark." Vertigon isnʼt just a city—itʼs a world engine, an urban leviathan sprawled across the living surface of Havalaea. Once the throne of the Goblin Empire and still its most iconic jewel, Vertigon blends arcological ambition, corporate decadence, ecological tension, and multiversal flux into a single impossible spire of civilization. From its rusted industrial roots in the south to the glass-smooth towers of the Highlands, Vertigon is both a history lesson and a prophecy in concrete. At its core, Vertigon represents the peak of Goblin ambition—a crossroads where technology, tradition, and ten thousand realities collide. It has survived regime changes, dimensional breaches, corporate coups, and elemental uprisings, and it remains a place where adventurers either rise to fame or vanish without a trace. Vertigon stretches beyond the vertical. Its body is a patchwork of arcologies, biodomes, market sprawls, and rewilded zones, each one shaped by a different era, purpose, or crisis. No single authority truly controls all of Vertigon, though many pretend to. Instead, power flows between royal agents, corporate councils, ecological orders, rebel enclaves, and undercity syndicates, each with their own vision of the cityʼs future. In the Orilaun Era—the age your campaign begins—Vertigon is no longer the center of the Empire, but it is still its heart. Portals open daily to distant realities. Market hubs trade in futures. Races thunder through the neon skyways. And in the cracks between arcologies, secrets older than the Empire fester or flourish. Whether youʼre a street-runner in the Neon Jungle, a diplomat in the Royal Sector, a poacher dodging Wardens in Malgeasia, or a void-scarred mage in Old South Bay—Vertigon has room for you. It may not welcome you. But it will change you.

Below the official economy runs a sprawling multiversal shadow market, offering what the legal world cannot. •The Midbay Outfit – Controls smuggling and unregistered shipping lanes. •Black Feathers – An information and espionage syndicate that sells secrets to the highest bidder. •The Crate Menagerie – Traffickers in rare creatures and exotic biologicals. •The Unnamed Syndicate – Whispers say they operate through dreams and disappearances, but no solid proof exists. These groups bribe officials, hack trade manifests, and often act as unofficial brokers between realities that refuse formal diplomacy.

Using Vertigon as a Campaign Hub Vertigon is more than a megacity—itʼs a multiversal engine of power, culture, and contradiction. It makes a powerful central hub for campaigns that need both narrative depth and logistical variety. Its internal districts span every tone and genre: from cyberpunk heights and neon arcologies to druidic enclaves and industrial ruins. Vertigon can support entire campaigns within its city limits, or serve as a launchpad into wider multiversal adventures. Players can rest, upgrade gear, argue cases in court, delve into shadowy districts, or prepare for dives into hell-realities—all without leaving the city. The city's transport networks (portal rails, sky lanes, and biodome corridors) also make it a perfect anchor for world-hopping parties. GMs can use Vertigon as a ‘home baseʼ that constantly evolves based on player choices, factional influence, or disasters. Vertigon as a Source of Faction Conflict Nearly every major multiversal power has a presence in Vertigon—whether as corporate offices, embassies, or black-market outposts.
